title: La Cage aux Folles at New York City Center #billyporter #waynebrady #...
transcript: It's been a great Encores season at New York City Center, but they saved the best for last. When the curtain rises on the opening number of La Cage aux Folles where each dancer is individually costumed as a Black icon, you know you're in for a treat. Based on the 1973 play, it's a musical farce full of classic Broadway earworms by Jerry Herman and a truly fantastic book by Harvey Fierstein. Wayne Brady and Billy Porter play this couple who've spent the last 20ish years together running a drag nightclub and raising their son Jean-Michel, who's now putting them in a sticky situation. He reveals he's getting married - to a woman, I might add - and that his fiancée's parents are conservative politicians. When he requests for the household to be de-queerified so that they can come over, he's essentially forcing his parents back into the closet. The jokes are nonstop in this somewhat far fetched musical, but it is quite poignant, especially in this moment in time. It's a show about family and visibility, and it's the chemistry between Wayne Brady and Billy Porter that elicits laughs and tugs at the heartstrings. The casting across the board is impeccable, from the leads to the supporting cast, especially the scene-stealing James Jackson Jr as the sassy housemaid, all the way through the ensemble which is fierce as hell. Yet for all of the show's glitz and glam, it's Billy Porter's raw and absolutely roof-raising “I Am What I Am” that leaves the biggest impression. As unapologetically present as he is, there's both a rousing and wrenching quality to his performance of that song specifically that feels remarkably confessional. It's as if he's saying, “I will not show up as anyone except for myself, but this authenticity does not come for free. It costs me something, and it is a heavy weight to bear.” I think that is something that a lot of queer people can relate to and is what makes the show perfect for Pride Month. La Cage aux Folles at City Center is a must-see, but it's only running through June 28th. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer explicitly calls it a 'must-see', praises casting 'across the board', highlights standout performances, and calls it the best of the Encores season.
keyQuote: La Cage aux Folles at City Center is a must-see
